blocks.html: These three points were of great consideration for the accused: for in the first place, much more faith is given to two witnesses who affirm some fact than to a thousand others a2. And next, in things which admit of some doubt, the favour either of the marriage, or of the children, or of the accused makes the balance fall (as was said a little before) to that side b2: with stronger reason, then, when all these favours present themselves together c.

notes.citation: Accursius (Accurse) on Digest 4.8.27.3 (De receptis: qui arbitrium receperint, l. Diem [proferre], § Si plures; Ulpian)
notes.original: Accurſe en la l. diem. P. ſi plures. D. de recep arb.
notes.gloss: The Gloss there weighs number against affirmation: two who affirm a fact outweigh many who deny it.

notes.citation: Digest 44.7 (De obligationibus et actionibus), l. Arrianus (cf. D. 44.7.47, Paul); Decretals X 2.27 (De sententia et re iudicata), the last chapter (chapter not identified)
notes.original: l. Arrianus. D de actio & oblig. c. fina. de re iud.
notes.gloss: Both cited at Annotation L, notes e and a: in doubt, the balance falls for the defendant and for the marriage.

notes.citation: Decretals X 2.20.33 (De testibus et attestationibus, c. Tam litteris; cited at annot-033 as iam literis) and X 2.20.47 (c. Licet ex quadam, Innocent III); X 4.14.7 (De consanguinitate et affinitate, c. Tua nos: hearsay testimony on degrees of kinship minus est validum; the c. rutela of annot-033)
notes.original: c. tam literis. c. licet cx quadam. de teſtib. c. tua. de conſang. & affinit.
notes.gloss: Hearsay makes no proof; the same chapters as annot-033 {a2}. The print's cx is ex. Translated in full at annot-053 {c}.

notes.citation: An authentica cited by the incipit Itaque, under a Code title printed C. con. de ſuc. (perhaps Communia de successionibus, C. 6.59) — not identified
notes.original: Aud. itaque. C. con. de ſuc.
notes.gloss: The transcription marks this note an orphan; it is the note for the body's third marker, read {c}. The print's Aud. is read as Aut., authentica. Its bearing on the concurrence of favours could not be verified.
